units.title: First crack
units.text: First crack marks a stage where internal pressure causes beans to audibly fracture as roasting reactions accelerate. The operator watches both sound and bean temperature rather than relying on sound alone.

units.title: Airflow adjustment
units.text: Increasing airflow helps carry smoke and chaff away from the roasting chamber while changing heat transfer through the bean mass. Adjustments are made gradually to avoid abrupt profile changes.

units.title: Rapid cooling
units.text: Roasted coffee is cooled promptly after discharge to slow further thermal development outside the drum. The cooling tray agitator remains running while the batch temperature falls.

units.title: Charge temperature
units.text: Charge temperature is selected before green coffee enters the drum because it influences the initial rate of heat transfer into the batch. It is recorded with the batch profile.

units.title: Chaff collector
units.text: The chaff collector is emptied and inspected regularly because accumulated dry chaff can restrict airflow and increase fire risk. The roaster is cool before the collector is serviced.

units.title: Post-roast rest
units.text: Freshly roasted coffee releases carbon dioxide for a period after roasting, so sealed packaging must account for continuing degassing. Flavor evaluation is scheduled consistently relative to roast date.
